recipe.history:
Feta is one of the oldest named cheeses in recorded history, with origins deeply embedded in the landscape and culture of Greece. The word itself likely derives from the Italian fetta, meaning slice, a term adopted by Greeks in the 17th century to describe a cheese that had been made in Greek and Balkan territories for millennia before it had a stable name. Homer mentions a cheese made from sheep's and goat's milk in the Odyssey — the Cyclops Polyphemus, whatever his faults, keeps a tidy dairy — and the tradition of aging fresh curd in brine is documented continuously throughout the Byzantine period and into the modern era. True PDO-protected Greek feta must be made in specific regions of Greece from the milk of sheep and goats that graze on local pastures, resulting in a cheese with a characteristic tang, creaminess, and minerality that comes directly from the terroir. Za'atar, the herb blend that accompanies this burger, is a similarly ancient Middle Eastern tradition: wild thyme, sumac, sesame seeds, and salt ground together into a fragrant seasoning that appears in Arab cookbooks from the medieval period and that has been dusted over flatbreads and mezze tables from Lebanon to Jordan to Palestine for centuries.

Whipped feta arrived on American menus as part of the broader wave of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cooking that swept through upscale casual dining in the 2010s. Chefs trained in or inspired by Levantine and Greek cuisines began offering whipped feta — blended smooth with olive oil, cream cheese, and lemon — as a dip and spread that was simultaneously more complex than cream cheese and less predictable than hummus. It found its way to the burger in the context of "Mediterranean-inspired" menus where the logic was simple: feta's saltiness and acidity play the same structural role as American cheese but with more personality. Roasted cherry tomatoes, which concentrate their natural sugars and acidity when blistered in a hot oven, became a natural companion — the concentrated tomato sweetness mirrors and amplifies what raw tomato does for a burger but with greater intensity. The za'atar-dusted pita-inspired bun completed a flavor profile that felt simultaneously ancient and entirely new.

I spent a summer in a rented apartment in Athens researching a food piece that never got published, and the meal I ate most frequently — sometimes twice a day — was a version of this sandwich from a hole-in-the-wall place near Monastiraki that had no name I could find in any guide. The cook would spread a thick layer of cold whipped feta onto grilled flatbread, pile it with slow-roasted tomatoes that had been left in the oven all morning, scatter za'atar over everything, and add whatever meat was on the spit or the griddle that day. I ate it standing at a counter next to locals who barely glanced at it. When I came home I spent three months figuring out how to translate those flavors into a burger, and the version I landed on felt like a fair homage to something that had no need of improvement.

There is no version of this burger — or any burger — that benefits from overcooking the patty. The whipped feta spread on this bun is cold, tangy, and creamy; the roasted tomatoes are sweet and acidic; the za'atar is herbal and nutty. Against all of that freshness and brightness, a dry, gray, well-done patty would be a categorical mistake. The medium rare center at 130–135°F provides the savory depth and juicy richness that anchors these vivid Mediterranean flavors, giving the whole assembly a gravitational center. The pink, yielding interior of the patty is as important to this burger's structure as the whipped feta itself — remove either one and you have something lesser.
ingredients: 1 egg beaten with 1 tbsp water (egg wash)
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (for the za'atar drizzle)
½ small red onion, very thinly sliced
instructions: 1. MAKE ZA'ATAR — Combine dried thyme, sumac, sesame seeds, oregano, and salt in a small bowl. Mix well and set aside. This makes more than needed — store the rest in an airtight jar.
2. MAKE THE PITA-INSPIRED BUNS — Combine flour, yeast, sugar, and salt in a stand mixer bowl.
3. Add warm water, warm milk, and olive oil. Mix with dough hook on low until combined, then medium speed for 8–10 minutes until smooth and slightly tacky.
4. Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
5. Divide into 4 portions, shape into balls, place on a parchment-lined sheet pan, flatten to about ¾ inch. Cover and proof 40 minutes.
6. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Brush with egg wash. Mix 2 tbsp za'atar with 1 tbsp olive oil and brush over the tops. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
7. Bake 15–17 minutes until golden. Cool on a wire rack.
8. ROAST THE CHERRY TOMATOES — Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C). Toss cherry tomatoes with olive oil, smashed garlic, thyme sprigs, sugar, salt, and pepper.
9. Spread on a rimmed baking sheet and roast 20–25 minutes until blistered, collapsed, and slightly caramelized. Remove garlic and thyme. Set aside.
10. MAKE THE WHIPPED FETA — Combine crumbled feta and softened cream cheese in a food processor. Blend until smooth.

11. With the processor running, drizzle in olive oil. Add lemon juice, lemon zest, grated garlic, and black pepper. Blend until very smooth and creamy. Taste — add more lemon juice or salt if needed. Refrigerate until assembly.

12. FORM THE PATTIES — Divide beef into 4 equal portions (about 170g each). Mix the salt, pepper, oregano, and cumin together and use to season the beef gently. Form into patties ¾-inch thick with a thumb dimple in the center.
13. COOK THE PATTIES — Heat a cast-iron skillet over high heat with a thin film of neutral oil until smoking.
14. Cook patties undisturbed 3 minutes until deeply browned on the bottom. Flip once.
15. Cook 2–2½ more minutes. Check internal temperature — target 130–135°F (54–57°C) for medium rare.
16. Remove and tent with foil. Rest 3 minutes.
17. TOAST THE BUNS — Split buns and toast cut-side down in the pan over medium heat, 60–90 seconds.
18. ASSEMBLE — Spread a generous layer of whipped feta on the bottom bun.
19. Arrange a few arugula leaves on the whipped feta.
20. Add a few thin red onion slices.
21. Set the patty on top.
22. Spoon roasted cherry tomatoes (with their juices) over the patty.
23. Dust with za'atar and a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil.
24. Finish with a pinch of fleur de sel.
25. Spread a thin layer of whipped feta on the top bun as well. Cap and serve immediately.
